keywords.def: (informal) make someone answer a difficult question or make a difficult decision in the moment, often embarrassing them in the process
(idiom) do things in your own way; think and behave differently from others
enjoy telling people what to do
allowed to do or have whatever someone (eg. a child) wants, usually with the result that they behave badly

sentences.en: Hello. This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好。这里是 BBC 英语教学的《6 Minute English》。

sentences.en: I’m Neil. And I’m Georgie. So, Georgie I’d like to know if you have any brothers and sisters, and if you get on well with them.
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔。我是乔治。乔治，我想知道你有没有兄弟姐妹，你和他们的关系好吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I do. I have a sister and we get on very well.
sentences.zh: 是的，我有。我有一个姐姐，我们关系非常好。

sentences.en: We didn’t used to but now that we’re adults we get on well.
sentences.zh: 我们以前关系一般，但现在长大了，关系就变得很好了。

sentences.en: Well, in this programme we’ll be discussing one of the closest relationships there is: the connection between sisters.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在今天的节目中，我们要讨论的是最亲密的关系之一：姐妹之间的纽带。

sentences.en: We’ll hear from three Irish sisters reuniting on a radio show, and from a psychotherapist on some stereotypes about sisterhood.
sentences.zh: 我们将听到三位在电台节目中重聚的爱尔兰姐妹的分享，以及一位心理治疗师关于姐妹情谊的一些刻板印象的见解。

sentences.en: Plus, we’ll be learning some useful new vocabulary too.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们还会学到一些实用的新词汇。

sentences.en: And remember, if you want to read along while you listen you can find the script for this programme on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 请记住，如果你想在听节目时对照阅读，可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到本期节目的文稿。

sentences.en: Yeah, great idea! Now, whether you have one or not, our history and culture is full of sisters, from the fairy tale of Cinderella and her ugly sisters to tennis players, Venus and Serena Williams.
sentences.zh: 太棒了！无论你有没有姐妹，我们的历史和文化中到处都是姐妹的身影，从灰姑娘和她丑陋的姐姐们的童话故事，到网球运动员维纳斯和小威廉姆斯。

sentences.en: And currently two sisters, Ellie and Rachel Reeves, are senior ministers in the British government.
sentences.zh: 目前还有两姐妹埃利和蕾切尔·里夫斯，她们是英国政府的高级大臣。

sentences.en: So, Neil, my question for you is this: what is Rachel Reeves' government job?
sentences.zh: 所以，尼尔，我的问题是：蕾切尔·里夫斯在政府中担任什么职务？

sentences.en: Is she: a) Home Secretary? b) Foreign Secretary? or c) Chancellor of the Exchequer?
sentences.zh: 她是：a) 内政大臣？b) 外交大臣？还是 c) 财政大臣？

sentences.en: Well I think the answer is c) the Chancellor of the Exchequer, which is the name of the finance minister in the UK.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为答案是 c) 财政大臣，也就是英国财政部长的头衔。

sentences.en: OK, Neil, we'll find out if that's the correct answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的，尼尔，我们稍后在节目中揭晓答案是否正确。

sentences.en: Nuala McGovern, the presenter of BBC Radio 4's Woman’s Hour, has two sisters.
sentences.zh: BBC Radio 4《Woman's Hour》节目的主持人努拉·麦戈文有两个姐姐。

sentences.en: They both live in Ireland so they're joining me on a video call.
sentences.zh: 她们都住在爱尔兰，所以正通过视频通话加入我的节目。

sentences.en: Hello Eileen. Hello Vera. Welcome to Woman’s Hour.
sentences.zh: 你好，艾琳。你好，维拉。欢迎来到《Woman's Hour》。

sentences.en: Hello. Hello. Nuala was born in Dublin and moved to New York then London to work as a journalist, while her two sisters stayed in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 你好。你好。努拉出生于都柏林，后来搬到纽约，又到伦敦当记者，而她的两个姐姐则留在了爱尔兰。

sentences.en: Here she introduces her older sister, Vera, and younger sister Eileen, for a BBC Radio 4 Woman's Hour special about sisterhood.
sentences.zh: 在这里，她向大家介绍了她的姐姐维拉和妹妹艾琳，这是一期关于姐妹情谊的 BBC Radio 4《Woman's Hour》特别节目。

sentences.en: Nuala was a little worried what her sisters would say about her on the radio, so let’'s listen in and find out: Eileen, what would you say if you were to describe our relationship as sisters?
sentences.zh: 努拉有点担心她的姐姐们会在电台上怎么评价她，所以我们一起来听听看：艾琳，如果要你形容我们作为姐妹的关系，你会怎么说？

sentences.en: Very connected, I think, and we do get on very well which I'm proud to say.
sentences.zh: 我觉得联系非常紧密，而且我们关系确实很好，我很自豪能这么说。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly. I’m going to put you on the spot, Vera.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。维拉，我要当面考考你了。

sentences.en: What word would you use to describe me as a sister?
sentences.zh: 你会用什么词来形容我这个妹妹（姐姐）呢？

sentences.en: I couldn't give you a word, but you definitely march to your own drum.
sentences.zh: 我找不出一个词来形容你，但你绝对是走自己的路。

sentences.en: What would that word be? Independent? Independent?
sentences.zh: 那个词会是什么？独立？独立吗？

sentences.en: Definitely. You like to control the situation.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。你喜欢掌控局面。

sentences.en: Eileen thinks she gets on with her sisters.
sentences.zh: 艾琳认为她和姐妹们相处得很好。

sentences.en: To get on with someone means to like them and have a good relationship with them.
sentences.zh: 与某人“get on”（相处）意味着喜欢他们并与他们保持良好的关系。

sentences.en: Nuala puts her older sister on the spot by asking Vera to describe her in one word.
sentences.zh: 努拉让维拉用一个词来形容她，从而把姐姐置于了尴尬的境地。

sentences.en: When you put someone on the spot, you make them answer a difficult question then and there, sometimes making them embarrassed or uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 当你“put someone on the spot”（让某人难堪/当场出丑）时，你会让他们当场回答一个难题，有时会让他们感到尴尬或不自在。

sentences.en: But Nuala didn't need to worry what her sisters would say - Vera simply said that Nuala marches to her own drum – she does things in her own way which may be different from how other people do things.
sentences.zh: 但努拉不需要担心姐姐们会说些什么——维拉只是说努拉我行我素（marches to her own drum）——她用自己的方式做事，这可能与其他人做事的方式不同。

sentences.en: It seems Vera, Nuala and Eileen have remained close friends as they've grown up, but the relationship between older, middle and younger sisters isn’t always so harmonious.
sentences.zh: 看来维拉、努拉和艾琳在长大的过程中一直保持着亲密的友情，但大姐、二姐和妹妹之间的关系并不总是那么和谐。

sentences.en: Let's listen to BBC Radio 4's Woman's Hour special programme as Nuala is joined by psychotherapist, Jennifer Gledhill: Thank you very much to Eileen and Vera.
sentences.zh: 让我们收听 BBC Radio 4《Woman's Hour》的特别节目，心理治疗师詹妮弗·格尔德希尔加入了努拉的访谈：非常感谢艾琳和维拉。

sentences.en: What a treat to have a chat with my sisters, about sisters!
sentences.zh: 能和我的姐妹们聊聊姐妹的话题，真是太棒了！

sentences.en: I want to bring in Jennifer here who's listening to it all.
sentences.zh: 我想请一直在听节目的詹妮弗加入进来。

sentences.en: Some of the stereotypes around siblings, that the elder sister is bossy, the middle sister is a peacemaker, and the little sister is spoiled - that is not applying to our family - but I'm wondering, is there any substance to that?
sentences.zh: 关于兄弟姐妹的一些刻板印象，比如大姐很专横，二姐是调解人，小妹妹被宠坏了——这在我们家并不适用——但我想知道，这些说法有依据吗？

sentences.en: Or why does that even get bandied around?
sentences.zh: 或者为什么这些说法会到处流传呢？

sentences.en: We love giving people labels, don't we? We like to put people into categories and then we can make sense of behaviours, but actually, since then, scientists find no, no proof of being these roles in families.
sentences.zh: 我们都喜欢给别人贴标签，不是吗？我们喜欢把人分类，这样就能理解他们的行为了，但实际上，从那以后，科学家发现并没有证据证明人们在家庭中扮演这些角色。

sentences.en: Nuala discusses stereotypes about siblings, a word that means either brother or sister.
sentences.zh: 努拉讨论了关于兄弟姐妹（sibling）的刻板印象，“sibling”这个词既可以指兄弟也可以指姐妹。

sentences.en: One stereotype is that the older sister is usually bossy – she enjoys telling people what to do.
sentences.zh: 其中一种刻板印象是，大姐通常很专横——她喜欢指挥别人做事。

sentences.en: Another stereotype is that the younger sister is spoiled.
sentences.zh: 另一种刻板印象是小妹妹被宠坏了。

sentences.en: If you describe a child as spoiled, you mean they are allowed to do anything they want, often with the result that they behave badly.
sentences.zh: 如果你把一个孩子描述为“spoiled”（被宠坏的），意思就是他们被允许做任何想做的事，这往往会导致他们行为恶劣。

sentences.en: What do you think about these stereotypes, Georgie?
sentences.zh: 乔治，你对这些刻板印象怎么看？

sentences.en: Are they true for you and your sister? I'm not sure I agree with these stereotypes because the older sister is meant to be bossy, but my younger sister is the bossy one.
sentences.zh: 它们在你和你的姐妹身上准吗？我不太确定我是否赞同这些刻板印象，因为按理说应该是大姐比较专横，但在我们家，我的妹妹才是那个专横的人。

sentences.en: I don’t think I’m bossy at all. Well, that’s interesting – Jennifer did say that there's no scientific proof.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己一点也不专横。嗯，这很有趣——詹妮弗确实说过这没有科学依据。

sentences.en: Anyway, it's time now to find out the answer to your question, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，现在是时候揭晓你的问题的答案了，乔治。

sentences.en: Yes, and my question was: What is Rachel Reeves' government job?
sentences.zh: 是的，我的问题是：蕾切尔·里夫斯在政府里做什么工作？

sentences.en: And you guessed she was the Chancellor of the Exchequer, which was… the correct answer!
sentences.zh: 而你猜她是财政大臣，这……回答完全正确！

sentences.en: Well done Neil. Hooray! OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've learned in this programme, starting with the phrasal verb, get on with someone, meaning to have a good relationship with them.
sentences.zh: 干得好，尼尔。太棒了！好了，让我们来回顾一下本期节目中学到的词汇，首先是动词短语“get on with someone”，意思是与某人关系良好。

sentences.en: If you put someone on the spot, you cause them embarrassment by forcing them to answer a difficult question at that very moment.
sentences.zh: 如果你“put someone on the spot”（把某人难堪），你就会强迫他们在当时回答一个困难的问题，从而让他们感到尴尬。

sentences.en: If you march to your own drum, you do things in your own unique way, regardless of how other people do them.
sentences.zh: 如果你“march to your own drum”（我行我素），你就会以自己独特的方式做事，不管别人怎么做。

sentences.en: A sibling can mean either a brother or sister.
sentences.zh: “Sibling”可以指兄弟或姐妹。

sentences.en: People who are bossy enjoy telling other people what to do.
sentences.zh: “Bossy”（专横的）人喜欢指挥别人做事。

sentences.en: And finally, a spoiled child is allowed to do whatever they want, becoming badly behaved as a result.
sentences.zh: 最后，“spoiled”（被宠坏的）孩子被允许做任何他们想做的事，结果导致他们的行为变得很差。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but remember to head over to bbclearningenglish.com where you can find loads more fun and helpful resources, including a worksheet and quiz for this programme.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们的六分钟节目时间又到了，但别忘了访问 bbclearningenglish.com，在那里你可以找到大量有趣且有用的资源，包括本期节目的练习纸和测验。

sentences.en: Bye for now! Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 先到这里！再见！
